Machine Learning
ES 335 · IIT Gandhinagar · Semester II, 2023–24
ES 335 is an introduction to machine learning: decision trees and ensembles, linear and logistic regression, gradient descent, neural networks and CNNs, nearest neighbours, unsupervised and reinforcement learning, and support vector machines. Most lectures link their slides, a full class recording and notebooks.

Questions
Is there a project?Not a separate one. Each assignment has a project-like question instead, the same for all students, such as building an activity classifier from public data and then from data you collect on your smartphone.
What are the prerequisites?There are no formal prerequisites, but you are expected to know Python programming and data structures (ES 242 or equivalent), probability and statistics, linear algebra and calculus. You must clear the prerequisite test to take the course.
What if I miss a quiz?A missed quiz is marked zero and there are no makeups, for any reason. Only the best three of four quizzes count, which is meant for exactly this case.
Is there a mid-semester or end-semester exam?Two of the four quizzes are held in the mid-semester and end-semester exam slots; the other two are held during the semester. All are closed book.
Can I use my laptop in class?No. Laptops are not allowed in class for any reason.

title: Questions
text:
Projects


Is there a project component in the course?

Yes and no. Each assignment has a project-like question. It is a more structured project in that sense, and all students get the same question. There is no separate project component: we feel this helps you understand the concepts covered in the course, and the added structure helps you get started.



Can you give an example of a project question?

We build an activity classifier (walking, running and so on). First we use publicly available datasets to build the classifier. Then we help you collect your own data with your smartphone and build a classifier on it. If you want to go beyond the learning objectives, you can deploy the classifier on your smartphone.

title: Questions
text:
Prerequisites


What are the course prerequisites?

Like all courses at IIT Gandhinagar, the course has no formal prerequisites. However, you are assumed to have a basic understanding of:

programming (Python) and data structures (ES 242 or equivalent);
probability and statistics;
linear algebra;
calculus.




What is the prerequisite test?

A test designed to make sure you have the background needed to take the course.



How can I prepare for the prerequisite test?

Your undergraduate course material should be sufficient. You may also use the preparation material listed under References on the home page.



What happens if I do not clear the prerequisite test?

You will not be allowed to take the course.



What does “clear” the test mean?

As in all courses at IIT Gandhinagar, the instructor decides the cut-off, and you have to score above it. The cut-off is not revealed to students in advance.

title: Questions
text:
Laptop policy


Can I use my laptop in class?

No. You are not allowed to use your laptop in class for any reason.

title: Questions
text:
Quizzes


What happens if I miss a quiz for any reason?

The quiz is marked zero. The best three of four quizzes count, a provision designed for such cases.



Are the quizzes and exams open book? Can I carry notes?

No. The exams and quizzes are closed book, and you may not carry notes.



How soon will I get my answer sheets back?

You should expect them back in four to five working days.



Is there a mid-semester or end-semester exam?

Two of the four quizzes are held in the mid-semester and end-semester exam slots. The other two are held during the semester.



Are the quizzes multiple-choice or written?

They may contain both multiple-choice and written questions.

title: Questions
text:
Assignments


What happens if I miss an assignment for any reason?

There are no extensions for assignments.



I have a doubt about an assignment. Whom should I write to?

Ask on the #assignments channel on Slack. If you do not get a response within two days, write to the instructor.



I do not know Python. Can I write the assignments in another language?

No. You have to use Python.



How are assignments evaluated?

Each assignment is followed by a viva. The TAs first check the code against the submission: any change from the submitted code is not allowed, and any instance earns a warning. The TAs then run the code and ask a few questions, about 75% on the assignment itself and about 25% on the theory behind the concepts it covers.
The marks are split as follows:

code runs correctly and solves the problem: 50%;
questions on the assignment and your understanding of the code: 25%;
code quality: 12.5%;
questions on the theory behind the concepts covered: 12.5%.




Are assignments individual or in groups?

In groups. All team members get the same grade for the assignment.

title: Questions
text:
Attendance


What is the attendance policy?

Attendance counts for 8% of the grade; see Attendance for how marks depend on the number of absences.

title: Questions
text:
Auditing


Can I audit the course?

You are free to attend the lectures. However, with a limited number of TAs and a large number of students, we cannot grade your submissions, and you cannot formally contribute to any team’s assignments.

title: Questions
text:
Computational resources


What computational resources are available?

Typically, the course has been kindly provided with Google Cloud credits, and this section is updated once the credits arrive. The credits can be used for your assignments and are more than sufficient for them.

Instructions

This test is open book, open internet, open notes. You can use any resources you want to solve the problems.
You should be typing your answers in a Jupyter notebook.
The submission would be a link to a public GitHub repository containing the notebook. Fill this form to submit your solution.
A random subset of students may have a viva post the exam. The viva would be based on the notebook and the solutions you have provided.
The test is open till 6th January 2024 9 PM. You can submit your solutions anytime before that.
This problem has to be solved individually. You cannot collaborate with anyone else.
The code should be written using Python.
Some questions may require you to answer in text. You can use markdown cells to write your answers. Some questions may require you to write code. You can use code cells to write your code. Some questions may require you to write mathematical expressions. You can use LaTeX to write your expressions. You can write such LaTeX expressions in markdown cells.
For any other questions, please ask on the General channel on Slack.




Questions

How many multiplications and additions do you need to perform a matrix multiplication between a (n, k) and (k, m) matrix? Explain.
Write Python code to multiply the above two matrices. Solve using list of lists and then use numpy. Compare the timing of both solutions. Which one is faster? Why?
Finding the highest element in a list requires one pass of the array. Finding the second highest element requires 2 passes of the the array. Using this method, what is the time complexity of finding the median of the array? Can you suggest a better method? Can you implement both these methods in Python and compare against numpy.median routine in terms of time?
What is the gradient of the following function with respect to x and y? \[
x^2y+y^3\sin(x)
\]
Use JAX to confirm the gradient evaluated by your method matches the analytical solution corresponding to a few random values of x and y
Use sympy to confirm that you obtain the same gradient analytically.
Create a Python nested dictionary to represent hierarchical information. We want to store record of students and their marks. Something like:

2022

Branch 1

Roll Number: 1, Name: N, Marks:

Maths: 100, English: 70 …


Branch 2

2023

Branch 1
Branch 2

2024

Branch 1
Branch 2

2025

Branch 1
Branch 2


Store the same information using Python classes. We have an overall database which is a list of year objects. Each year contains a list of branches. Each branch contains a list of students. Each student has some properties like name, roll number and has marks in some subjects.
Using matplotlib plot the following functions on the domain: x = 0.5 to 100.0 in steps of 0.5.

\(y = x\)
\(y = x^2\)
\(y = \frac{x^3}{100}\)
\(y = \sin(x)\)
\(y = \frac{\sin(x)}{x}\)
\(y = \log(x)\)
\(y = e^x\)

Using numpy generate a matrix of size 20X5 containing random numbers drawn uniformly from the range of 1 to 2. Using Pandas create a dataframe out of this matrix. Name the columns of the dataframe as “a”, “b”, “c”, “d”, “e”. Find the column with the highest standard deviation. Find the row with the lowest mean.
Add a new column to the dataframe called “f” which is the sum of the columns “a”, “b”, “c”, “d”, “e”. Create another column called “g”. The value in the column “g” should be “LT8” if the value in the column “f” is less than 8 and “GT8” otherwise. Find the number of rows in the dataframe where the value in the column “g” is “LT8”. Find the standard deviation of the column “f” for the rows where the value in the column “g” is “LT8” and “GT8” respectively.
Write a small piece of code to explain broadcasting in numpy.
Write a function to compute the argmin of a numpy array. The function should take a numpy array as input and return the index of the minimum element. You can use the np.argmin function to verify your solution.
